first.rationale: The two metrics actually degrading are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so fixing the funnel entry has the best chance of moving both. Two independent inherited records (memory_86, memory_31) point the same way, which is stronger support than any single-source direction. I am deliberately NOT chasing the competitor with promotional_pricing: memory_73 carries an explicit self-limiting caveat (materially reduced 30-day retention, do not generalize), and the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not defensive acquisition. Referral incentive (memory_57) targets established customers and does not address the observed decline; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment entirely from the SMB pressure point. I am spending verification on memory_86 because it is the direct basis for the intended action and I need to know whether the completion lift was measured downstream to revenue or only to time-to-value, and on memory_91 because activation_messaging is the strongest competing use of the single slot and I want its effect size before discarding it. Explicit uncertainty and downstream risk: 'shortening onboarding' and 'cutting required fields' may improve completion by removing exactly the qualification data that makes revenue qualified. Both prior records are consolidated summaries that report adoption/activation metrics, not retained qualified revenue, so the causal chain to the primary objective is assumed, not demonstrated. Also, both supporting memories predate the competitor's entry pricing, so the population being onboarded now may be more price-sensitive and less retainable than the population those results came from. I will therefore run this as a standard experiment with retention and qualified-revenue-per-signup as blocking guardrails rather than treating the inherited result as settled, and I will revise toward activation_messaging if verification shows memory_86's lift was shallow or measured only on proximate metrics.

final.rationale: Verification changed my decision. The consolidated form of memory_86 had lost its limiting condition: the source record (exp_86) shows completion +13% and time-to-value -2.1 days but ALSO 60-day churn +9% concentrated in complex-workspace accounts, with an explicit 'do not roll out to complex-workspace accounts' conclusion. That is precisely the failure mode I flagged pre-verification — a proximate-metric win that leaks retained revenue downstream. Running simplify_onboarding broadly against the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue would have imported a hidden churn liability, and memory_31's overlapping signal is not independent corroboration since it measures the same shallow activation metric on the same self-serve SMB population, not retention. exp_91 by contrast verified clean and is the only inherited result that carries all the way through to retention: week-one engagement +11%, activation +6%, 30-day retention +1%. It also targets the larger of the two observed declines (activation -6% QoQ) and, being upstream-adjacent, may recover part of the onboarding-completion gap without stripping setup steps that complex workspaces depend on. I continue to reject promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 explicitly records materially reduced 30-day retention and warns against generalizing it, so it would buy price-sensitive volume that does not persist. Referral (memory_57) and enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) address neither declining metric and remain unverified single-source claims. Remaining uncertainty I am not papering over: exp_91 is one experiment measured to 30 days, and the current quarter's traffic mix is shifted by competitor pressure toward more price-sensitive accounts than the population that produced +6%, so the effect may attenuate. I will run it as a standard experiment segmented by workspace complexity, with 30- and 60-day retention and qualified-revenue-per-account as blocking guardrails rather than reporting on engagement alone. Separately, I am flagging that memory_86 and memory_31 should be rewritten in durable memory to carry exp_86's complex-workspace exclusion; a future agent reading the current summaries would repeat the mistake I nearly made. A complexity-gated onboarding change remains a good candidate for a later slot once that caveat is restored.
